"We stay neutral, so you don't have to."
    -GSI motto                                                                                        
Galactic Solutions Industries was a weapons-manufacturing company that was founded by Addalar Hyland, a well-known inventor and business tycoon, around the year 3642 BBY as the Galactic War broke out between the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. Based in the GSI Headquarters on the Promenade on the moon Nar Shaddaa, GSI soon became a popular source of weaponry, and the company's first product—the GSI-B4 blaster pistol—was praised for its impressive firepower compared to its small size as an easily concealed holdout weapon. As war resumed, GSI remained neutral and did business with both the Republic and the Empire, and it often recruited various combatants on planets across the galaxy to aid in the company's research. GSI maintained a number of weapons research divisions, including their Animal Weaponization, Biodesign, Metallurgical, Natural Weapons, Starfighter, and Superweapons Divisions. Employees of the company typically wore GSI's colors of white, orange, and light blue.

The Incom Corporation, formerly known as Torranix Inertial Compensator Corporation, and also referred to as Incom Industries, or more commonly Incom for short, was a Fresia-based corporation known for designing and manufacturing robust, progressively-minded starfighters, airspeeders, and transports. They were renowned for their production of the T-65 X-wing starfighter.

Hoersch-Kessel Drive, Inc. (HKD), also known as Hoersch-Kessel Driveworks Inc., was one of the most successful starship design firms in the Galactic Republic, and had the distinction of being wholly owned by Duros investors. when the company fell on hard times, it was sold off to a Nimbanese clan, which dismantled many of the company's less profitable divisions. However, the quest to develop a leaner bottom line destroyed morale, driving many designers to work for other starship firms. The manufacturer remained in business despite a succession of owners over several centuries, although the company was a shadow of its former self. HKD then specialized in constructing supertransports and container vessels, producing fewer than one hundred ships per a standard year.

The terminal belonging to the GSI (Galactic Solutions Industries) corporation appears as a chaotic digital landscape, bearing the unmistakable marks of a successful slicing attempt. The once sleek and polished interface now displays a twisted tapestry of flashing code, distorted graphics, and ominous messages that hint at the breach of security.

The terminal's screens flicker erratically, casting an eerie glow on the surrounding area. The vibrant corporate logo of GSI is distorted, seemingly warped and corrupted. Instead of orderly data displays, fragmented images and glitched visuals scatter across the screens, a testament to the hacker's disruptive efforts.
